**Finding resubmitted: Compliant** — no redline, no comment (correct output for a compliant finding).

The repair addressed the one flagged item, the deterministic "period ≥ 90 days" check:

- **Root cause was phrasing, not substance.** I searched the document for the period language and confirmed § 19.2 is the only statement of the warranty term, and it spells the number out — "For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later" — with no digit form anywhere. That is exactly the 90-day preferred floor, and the "whichever is later" trigger runs longer than a delivery-date-only measure.
- **Quote tightened** to lead with the duration sentence and carry through the Hosted Services sentence, so the period and the software-side coverage sit inside the cited text.
- **Rationale now states the duration finding explicitly** — ninety days in words = 90 days, at the threshold rather than below it — and flags that a numeric screen misses it only because of the spelled-out numeral.
- **Software benchmark tied to the definition**: § 1.8 defines "Services" to include the hosted software, and § 19.2 warrants Hosted Services conform *throughout the subscription term*, an open-ended full-term warranty that meets or exceeds the 12-month software position.

Everything else the verifier confirmed is retained and now cited more precisely: the professional/workmanlike and conformance standards (§ 19.1, § 3.1), compliance with law and no malicious code (§ 19.3), the re-perform/repair/replace-then-refund remedy that is expressly non-exclusive for key claim types (§ 19.4), and the implied-warranty-only disclaimer that affirmatively preserves express warranties (§ 19.5). I also noted that § 21.4 does not convert § 19.4 into a sole remedy and that § 6 supports the warranty trigger.

The only narrowing remains the malicious-code warranty limited to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor" — customary, and not worth a redline against an otherwise at-or-above-preferred package.
